clue.text: Could be every cent paid me

definitions.text: Could be every cent paid me

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the following words may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tallies the money handed over, hoping every last cent has reached them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: the letters of EVERY CENT PAID ME, rearranged, give a phrase that describes them when read normally.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor collecting every cent owed would note that settlement in full has come in.

clue.text: Two comparative dunces need careful handling in geometry lesson

definitions.text: Two comparative dunces need careful handling in geometry lesson

parts.words: Two comparative dunces need careful handling in geometry lesson
parts.note: a pun: two (a pair) of 'comp.' (comparative) 'asses' (dunces) describes the pointed drawing instrument used in geometry, which must be handled carefully

explanation.surface: A teacher warns that two slow pupils being compared must be handled gently in a maths class.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the instrument's name as PAIR OF COMP ASSES: comp. is an abbreviation for comparative and asses are dunces.
explanation.definitionFit: The geometry instrument for drawing circles has a sharp point, so pupils must handle it with care.

clue.text: How it stands with the Sun said to determine drinking time

definitions.text: How it stands with the Sun said to determine drinking time

parts.words: How it stands with the Sun said to determine drinking time
parts.note: the saying 'the sun is over the ...' means it is late enough in the day for an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone checks the sun's position to decide whether it is time for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The old naval saying 'the sun is over the yardarm' marks the time when a drink is permitted; the clue describes the spar the sun is judged against.
explanation.definitionFit: The spar on a ship's mast is what the sun must climb above, by tradition, before drinks are poured.

clue.text: Long stories about single US politician — 25 could be one

definitions.note: the definition is singular in sense though the answer is plural; cholera (25) is an example of a widespread outbreak

indicators.note: about means the long stories are wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: epics are long narrative tales
Dem is short for a Democrat in US politics
single is one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Long tales are told about one lone American politician.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMI goes inside EPICS after its third letter. The definition refers to 25-across, CHOLERA, an example of such outbreaks; the singular 'one' sits loosely with the plural answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera has caused many widespread outbreaks of disease, so it is an example of the kind of illness behind them.

clue.text: What's on your to-do list? First of ten questions

indicators.note: first of means take only the opening letter of the word ten

parts.note: to question someone is to ask them; asks is the verb form

explanation.surface: A list-keeper wonders what is on today's agenda, starting with ten questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Jobs to be done are the items written on a to-do list.

clue.text: Strange half-animal with needle-like teeth?

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are odd and rearranged into another order
half means keep just one half of the word animal, its second three letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A weird creature, half animal, has teeth as sharp as needles.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the second half of ANIMAL, MAL, add NEEDLE and rearrange. The whole clue also suggests teeth coated in hard glaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth carry a hard glossy coating, so a creature with fine sharp teeth has glazed, coated ones.

clue.text: Sailor nearly holds sign up the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way says the hidden letters must be read backwards
holds means the letters are contained within the words Sailor nearly

explanation.surface: A sailor almost hangs a notice upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor' tempts as AB or TAR, but it is just part of the hiding place: the letters run across the end of Sailor into nearly, then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To register as a member or student is to put your name down, the same as enlisting.

clue.text: Old Tommy in TA, never in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier in the Territorial Army is never in any trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tommy is a British private soldier; the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: An old soldier who has served long is called by this term for an experienced former serviceman.

clue.text: Cat jumpy after running off — a Cheshire cat's speciality

indicators.note: after places the rearranged cat behind the vanishing word

parts.note: running off means vanishing or leaving

indicators.note: jumpy suggests the letters jump about into another order

explanation.surface: A nervous cat bolts, as a Cheshire cat famously would.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cheshire Cat in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland fades away until only its grin remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat in Lewis Carroll's story is known for vanishing gradually, a trick of fading from view.

clue.text: Broken-down, one enters fashionable races

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

indicators.note: enters means one goes inside the word for races

parts.note: runs are races
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A worn-out horse is entered into smart races.
explanation.definitionFit: A building that has fallen to pieces is described as being in a ruined state.

clue.text: Charges with gas and water reversed around a percentage

indicators.note: around means the backwards water wraps the percentage
reversed means the word for water is read backwards

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
a percentage is a rate, such as an interest rate

explanation.surface: Someone fills things with gas and reverses the water flow around a percentage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like fees or accusations, but here it means fills, as a soda siphon is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy drinks are made by forcing air or carbon dioxide into a liquid, filling it with gas.

clue.text: Old wise man of Native American tribe

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: An elderly wise man belongs to a Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American nation of the Great Plains, now based in Oklahoma.

clue.text: Explosion of saltpetre could take your leg off

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters of saltpetre apart into a new order

explanation.surface: Saltpetre, a gunpowder ingredient, could blow your leg off if it went up.
explanation.walkthrough: Saltpetre is potassium nitrate, used in gunpowder, which makes 'Explosion' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprung metal jaw set to catch animals can sever a limb, so it describes the device.

clue.text: Give a short speech at burial service

parts.note: to commit is to give or hand over

indicators.note: short means cut off the final letter of the word for speech

parts.note: a talk is a speech

explanation.surface: A mourner is asked to say a few words at a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'a short speech', the 'a' and 'at' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The committal is the part of a funeral when the body is lowered into the grave or consigned.

clue.text: Favour that owners may do vis- à-vis their pets

definitions.meaning: to favour a parent is to resemble them

definitions.text: that owners may do vis- à-vis their pets
definitions.meaning: owners are said to grow to resemble their pets, or literally to follow behind them on walks

explanation.surface: Pet owners are said to come to look like their animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Resembling a relative in looks is the sense of favouring them, as in a child favouring a parent.

clue.text: Part of speech in German that's pivotal

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A crucial word in a German speech hinges the whole sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A door turns on the jointed metal pivot that holds it, so the part is literally pivotal.

clue.text: Staying cool, he starts to attack the evidence

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letters of attack and the

parts.note: proof is evidence

explanation.surface: A calm detective keeps his head as he begins to tackle the evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish or material that resists high temperature stays unaffected, so it keeps cool under fire.

clue.text: Indicates an unpopular test

definitions.meaning: to indicate is to signify, as in 'that signifies trouble'
the ... test, which checks income before benefits are paid, is widely disliked; the word alone stands for it

explanation.surface: Someone signals that a test is unpopular.
explanation.walkthrough: A means test in Britain assesses a person's income before state benefits are granted, which made it notoriously disliked.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate something is to signify it, and the second sense is the word naming an income check.

clue.text: I learn nothing about flight control

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A student pilot admits learning nothing about how to control a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinged flaps on an aircraft's wings control its roll, a key part of the flight controls.

clue.text: Tease your Head — he might lock you away!

parts.note: to kid is to tease
napper is old British slang for the head

explanation.surface: A pupil is told to tease the headteacher, who might keep them in detention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a headteacher, but it is slang for the head on your shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: An abductor seizes a victim and holds them captive, often locked up until ransom is paid.

clue.text: High 23 in China, perhaps, with gold

definitions.note: 23-across gives a level stretch of land; a high one is raised

parts.note: a plate is an example of china crockery
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A high plain in China is rich in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it means crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevated stretch of level ground is a raised flatland, which is the meaning given here.

clue.text: Everyone gets blasé, say, about a departure announcement

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: say means the word for blasé is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: someone blasé is bored, unimpressed by anything

explanation.surface: Everyone grows weary waiting for the departure call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here is a link word showing the pieces gather around the A; the order of the answer places A before the spoken word.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard or conductor shouts this call to tell passengers to get on before a train or ship leaves.

clue.text: Female support at home, located in 18 partly

definitions.note: the organ sits in the head, the napper part of 18-across

parts.note: a bra is a woman's support garment
in means at home

explanation.surface: A woman supports someone at home, somewhere within the kidnapper.
explanation.walkthrough: 18-across ends in NAPPER, slang for the head, which is where the organ is located.
explanation.definitionFit: The thinking organ lives inside the skull, and the skull is the head referred to in 18.

clue.text: Russian retreat leads to defiant action confronting heavy artillery

indicators.note: leads to means take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A Russian army's withdrawal leads to bold action against big guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' wants to be a military withdrawal; here it is a place to get away to.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country cottage used as a summer escape from the city.

clue.text: Simple, undecorated yet homely flat

definitions.meaning: homely, in the American sense, means unattractive in looks
a flat stretch of land, such as a prairie

explanation.surface: A modest flat is simple and unadorned, yet cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: Four definitions in a row; 'flat' looks like an apartment but means level land.
explanation.definitionFit: Each word is a sense of the one answer: uncomplicated, unadorned, not attractive, and level ground.

clue.text: Sancho Panza eg was not entirely eagle-eyed

indicators.note: not entirely means part of the word for eagle-eyed is dropped, here its opening two letters

parts.note: someone eagle-eyed is sharply observant

explanation.surface: Don Quixote's squire, Sancho Panza, was not always sharp-sighted.
explanation.walkthrough: Sancho Panza is Don Quixote's squire in Cervantes' novel. 'was' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A squire attends his master, so Sancho Panza is an example of an attendant in domestic employ.

clue.text: Puncture in dodgy car could prove fatal

indicators.note: in means the hole goes inside the rearranged car
dodgy suggests the letters are unreliable and rearranged

parts.note: a puncture is a hole

explanation.surface: A puncture in a dodgy car could lead to a fatal crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to a road accident; the definition is the disease, which can kill.
explanation.definitionFit: The waterborne disease often kills victims through dehydration, so it is something that may be deadly.

clue.text: Deep split might cause the downfall of Hollywood

definitions.text: Deep split might cause the downfall of Hollywood

parts.words: Deep split might cause the downfall of Hollywood
parts.note: a geological crack in California that could trigger an earthquake destroying Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A deep rift could ruin the film industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' looks like a quarrel within the film industry; it is a crack in the earth running through California.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Californian crack in the earth's crust runs near Los Angeles and could bring a devastating earthquake.
